items.title: Spiegle Willcox and Al Gallodoro interviewed by Monk Rowe, Norwich, New York, November 14, 1995
items.q: Howard Vorhees... he picked me up, we did the job... with about a five or six piece group

ctx.x: You know this is something funny. He has a fantastic memory. Everybody says, “Al, how do you remember sixty years ago?” I say you can’t remember everything, but a lot of things are just like it happened today. Like the day that I got my first job in New Orleans. Howard Vorhees. I went to his house and noodled and this and that, and he says, “Yeah, © Fillius Jazz Archive -7-

kid, I’m going to hire you.” Beverly Gardens was a gambling house. They didn’t call them casinos then. A gambling house with about a five or six piece group, and he picked me up, now this was 1927. He picked me up, we did the job, coming home he pats me, he says, “Kid you did a very good job, I’m going to up you to fifty dollars a week.” That was—
